title: Cheverus field hockey outlasts Thornton Academy in A South nailbiter
text:
Our Communities. Our Teams. Our Future.
We’re proud to make high school sports coverage free for everyone, because these moments matter. At Maine State Credit Union, we’re here for the people and places that make Maine strong. Let’s go! Learn more at mainestatecu.org. 
SCARBOROUGH — The game, the season and the Cheverus field hockey team’s aura of invincibility were on the line. And Sydney Brunelle wanted them all on her stick.
In the Stags’ first corner of the post-overtime session in the Class A South final, officials awarded a penalty stroke that could make official their sixth straight trip to the state championship game.
Brunelle wanted the shot. Badly.
“I told coach, ‘Please, this is my senior year. I know I can do it. I can capitalize,'” she said.
She was right. Brunelle scored to give top-ranked Cheverus a 2-1 win over No. 3 seed Thornton Academy on Wednesday night at Scarborough High School, punching the Stags’ ticket back to the state final and keeping alive their pursuit of a fourth consecutive championship.
Cheverus will face North champion Mt. Ararat in the state title game Saturday at Edward Little High School in Auburn.
“I think I’m not going to be able to go to sleep tonight,” Brunelle said. “The entire team played their entire heart out. The message from the coaches and the captains was don’t leave anything out there. You have your entire season left on the line.”
Cheverus (17-0) stretched its winning streak to 34 games and its unbeaten streak to 71, but the Stags’ path to their latest state final hasn’t looked like the previous journeys. After rolling with a dominant offense in previous years, this Cheverus team has endured one stressful test after another, needing overtime to beat Sanford/Kennebunk and Thornton (13-4) in the previous two rounds of the playoffs.
But while opponents have found the formula to push the Stags, they are still looking for a way to beat them.
“When you’re fighting all the way up through, my hope is that it prepares you for the next game even better,” coach Andrea Musante said. “I feel like they were made for this moment. They played with pure heart all the way through this game.”
Thornton came close to ending the Stags’ streaks. After a slow start, the Golden Trojans came out fighting in the fourth quarter and got a tying goal from Shyla McVeigh, then had some chances for a walk-off goal in the first and second overtimes.
“We started a little bit shaky, because it was definitely uncharted territory for a lot of us, myself included,” Trojans coach Lexie Carter said. “But before the game, I told the girls that no matter what, I’m proud of them. … Getting here was never really the goal. But now that we’re here, let’s make it count.”
A tie through two overtimes meant the teams went to corners to decide the winner. Ava Martin and Brunelle broke up Thornton’s first try. On the first attempt by Cheverus, Brunelle found her sister, Brooke, for a shot that a Trojans defender illegally stopped with her torso behind the goalie.
On the penalty stroke, Brunelle, one of two finalists for the Miss Maine Field Hockey award, calmly fired the ball inside the left post, then leapt high in the air before turning to embrace her teammates.
“I knew that if I shot fast enough, she wasn’t going to be able to get it,” she said. “I had been practicing it, and I just needed the confidence to be able to do it.”
Such dramatics didn’t seem in store early, when freshman Avery Tinker scored on a corner with 8:37 left in the second quarter, and Cheverus spent the first three quarters suffocating the Trojans’ attack.
But in the fourth, Thornton found life. The Trojans began entering the Cheverus end and generating corners, and they cashed in on their last one when Olivia Lamey inserted to Camila Sibille, who found McVeigh for a shot that tied the score with 8:39 left.
“It was tough. Going into it, I told the girls this is going to be the hardest game you’ve played, probably ever, and probably ever will play,” Carter said. “I think we started to pick up and pay attention to the simple stuff.”
Both teams had chances in overtime. Sydney Brunelle and Tinker had opportunities in the first overtime, and Thornton just missed an Addie Lamey-to-Sibille connection in the second OT.
Sibille had the ball heading toward the Cheverus net with about 5:30 left in the second overtime, but Ava Martin, a defensive force all game, stuck with her and prevented a good look.
“Our adrenaline is high right now, we’re on top of the word,” said Martin, a senior captain. “I think we never had doubts. … We stood our ground and played a really strong, composed game.”

title: Above Average Highs Thursday With Afternoon Showers Possible
text:
BANGOR, Maine (WABI) - In the wake of a warm front, conditions will remain on the mild side tonight. Expect mostly clear skies with light southwest winds. Lows settle into the 40s to low 50s, running well above normal for early November. Patchy fog will be possible especially in The County.
Thursday: Increasing Clouds, Scattered PM Showers
Thursday begins with filtered sunshine before cloud cover rapidly thickens during the morning hours. Highs climb into the 60s—roughly 10° to 15° above average. A cold front tracking west to east brings light showers. The west will see the steadiest rainfall. As the showers move east expect them to weaken and fizzle out. Highest totals will be in the west where up to 0.25″ is possible. As you go east totals taper off with those from the Bangor region into Downeast will only see a few hundredths of an inch.
Friday: Cloudy, Rain Later In The Day
The cold front stalls just offshore early Friday morning, guiding broken showers along coastal communities before drying out by midmorning. Expect mostly cloudy skies region-wide with highs in the low to mid-60s. Rain chances ramp up Friday evening as an area of low pressure rides northeastward along the front, bringing wet weather to the coast first before spreading inland overnight. How far north the low tracks will dictate how far inland the rain makes it.
Weekend: Cool-Down and Soaking Rain
Rain continues into Saturday morning, gradually turning lighter and more showery through the afternoon as the low moves through the Gulf of Maine. Cooler air filters in, holding Saturday highs in the low to mid-50s. Scattered showers linger into Sunday with highs cooling further into the 40s to low 50s before the system departs.
Rainfall totals look to be highest along the coast and Downeast where an average of 1-2″ of rain is possible. As you go farther north and west, totals will be drop off with communities in the Western Mountains expecting less than 0.5″.

title: Cape Elizabeth girls soccer earns chance to defend its state title

Our Communities. Our Teams. Our Future.

FALMOUTH — Alice DeGeorge says an opponent scoring a goal is just fuel for the Cape Elizabeth girls soccer team.
That’s the way it worked in the Class B South final Wednesday night. The defending state champions fell behind rival Yarmouth early in the second half, then responded with two goals in less than four minutes, then added another for a 3-1 victory.
“We come out so much fiercer in the second half, and we don’t get down on ourselves when people score on us. It’s our fire,” said DeGeorge, a right back who gets involved in the offense.
Cape Elizabeth (15-1-1), which won last year’s Class B title, will face North champion John Bapst in the state final Saturday at Cameron Stadium in Bangor. Yarmouth finished 14-3.
SETTING THE STAGE
These Western Maine Conference powers have been on a collision course since Yarmouth won the season opener 1-0 that avenged a 2-0 loss in last season’s B South final.
Cape Elizabeth, the top seed in B South, had not lost since and outscored opponents 74-5 with 12 shutouts, including a 2-0 win at home against Yarmouth in the Oct. 3 rematch.
Second-seeded Yarmouth (14-2) had one late-season loss to Greely but otherwise rolled, outscoring opponents 66-6 with 11 shutout wins.
HOW IT HAPPENED
The Clippers controlled the play in the first half and had all the best chances but the match was scoreless at the break.
Fiona John, one of the nine senior starters for Yarmouth, changed that when she ran onto a slick pass through the middle from Lilah Pernal and was able to slot her shot past Cape goalie Kelsie Law and inside the right post with 36:41 left in the game.
Less than two minutes later, Cape responded when freshman wing Pippi Hooper read a midfield pass, intercepted it, and immediately used her speed to go to goal. Yarmouth keeper Julia Soelberg had a solid deflection of Hooper’s hard shot but not enough to keep it from banging off the far post and into the net with 35:15 to play.
“When I got the ball, I saw the net in front of me and I knew I had to take it because I had no other options. There was no one with me so I just had to go,” Hooper said. “I just let my feet take me. I don’t really think in those moments. I just saw the net and I knew I had to shoot it.”
Barely more than two minutes later, Cape junior midfielder Haisel McGeachey put a direct kick from the left side into a dangerous spot. Soelberg got to it and deflected the ball off the underside of the crossbar, but as she went to secure the ball, with DeGeorge steaming toward her, it squirted free and into the net.
“We chased from there because that’s what we had to do,” said Clippers first-year coach Matt Morrill. Yarmouth was also without forward Miah Jacobs, one of the top sprinters in Maine and a hard-to-handle presence on the soccer field. Jacobs was injured in Yarmouth’s semifinal win against Greely.
Alexa Mallory of Cape Elizabeth finished the scoring when she stayed with a play, tracking down the ball near the end line and then connecting on a tough angle shot with 5:55 to play.
“We never give up. That’s our saying,” Mallory said.
STATISTICS
• Yarmouth: Fiona John, 1 goal; Lilah Pernal, 1 assist; Julia Soelberg, 3 saves; Team, 10 shots (5 on goal), five corner kicks.
• Cape Elizabeth: Pippi Hooper, 1 goal; Alexa Mallory, 1 goal; Kelsie Law, 5 saves; Team, 10 shots (6 on goal), 1 corner kick.
